Θέατρο

ΤΟΥΡΝΑΣ - ΤΣΑΚΝΗΣ RADIO CITY

Τετάρτη 11 Φεβρουαρίου στις 20:00 | IT Athens

The guitar tone cuts through the room before you've found your place. IT Athens is filling with the particular energy of a Greek rock audience waiting for two of the genre's most significant voices. You smell cigarettes from the smoking area, hear the murmur of anticipation in mixed conversations.

Tournas and Tsaknis share history that reaches back to the foundations of Greek rock. Both emerged from the scene that defined what rock could sound like in Greek, when the language was still being bent to fit amplified music. They've taken different paths since, Tournas toward folk-rock contemplation, Tsaknis toward political edge. Tonight they share a stage.

The Radio City billing suggests a night that acknowledges influence, pays homage to sources while maintaining artistic identity. When Greek rock musicians invoke Radio City, they're referencing a particular mythology of American music, the idea of a glamorous broadcast reaching across oceans. The irony isn't lost on anyone.

Tournas's voice carries decades of Greek music through its weathered texture. He's sung protest songs and love ballads, folk arrangements and rock experiments. The material draws from a catalog that most Greek households could hum. Tsaknis brings sharper edges, lyrics that haven't lost their political bite, songs that address Greek reality without apology.

The IT Athens crowd for this pairing reflects the generational reach of both artists. You'll find people who bought these albums when they were new, who remember where they were when certain songs first played on the radio. Alongside them are younger listeners who inherited the music, for whom these songs provide connection to a Greece they never directly experienced.

IT Athens provides the appropriate container. The venue sits in Exarchia, a neighborhood that's kept its edge while the rest of Athens gentrifies. The sound system handles the dynamic range these performers require, the room shaped for attention rather than background noise.

If you need trendy international acts and cutting-edge sounds, this evening operates in different territory. Tournas and Tsaknis belong to Greek rock history, their significance inseparable from their context. But if you're ready to hear what Greek rock becomes when its significant voices share a stage, when decades of material converge in a single evening, when the weight of the tradition becomes audible, you find your way to Exarchia.
